newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian wool prices seen firm this week.
newsitem.headline: Australian wool prices seen firm this week.

text.p: Australian wool prices are expected to remain firm when sales resume this week, Wesfarmers Dalgety Ltd said.
Sales this week are in Sydney and Fremantle with a small offering of only 79,400 bales on offer, 43,500 bales in Sydney and 35,900 bales in Fremantle.
The eastern market indicator rose 10 cents to end the week to July 4, before the recess, at 716 cents a kg clean, up sharply from 598 cents a year ago.
The western market indicator fell 27 cents to 665 cents.
Wesfarmers said there were only an average of 70,000 bales rostered for sale during the month of August.

Wool International would not be under selling pressure having already sold 70 percent more than the minimum sales required to fill the September quarter quota. Wool production for the 1997/98 season was also again expected to be relatively low.
"These factors all indicate a positive outlook for the start of 1997/98 sales period," Wesfarmers said.
